  "text": "The constable tried to pull away. Ada held fast.

“That wasn’t there,” he said.

On the street, the child turned her head a little. Not enough for them to see her face. Rain passed through her hair and struck the pavement beneath.

Venn crouched beside the carved name. “There’s room for another.”

The five letters began to climb. Their wooden corners clicked against each stair, slow and deliberate. Ada opened her hand. The sixth letter lay still, its grain darkening where her skin had touched it.

“May I leave?” asked the voice beneath the hood.

The constable shut his eyes. “She used to ask me that when I locked the garden gate.”

“Your daughter?” Ada said.

“Yes.” He looked toward the street. “But she’s grown now.”

The child outside raised one hand. It held a key.

Ada felt the letter shift against her palm, turning its carved face toward the open door. Beneath Mara’s name, a second line emerged, cut so deeply that pale curls of wood fell onto the stair. It was not the daughter’s name. It was the constable’s.

Venn backed away. “Don’t let it reach the water.”

The coat bent toward them. Its empty hood came level with Ada’s face, and the small voice spoke again, softer this time.

“I’m asking you.”

Ada set the letter on the dry stair above the others. “Then tell us who’s waiting outside.”

For the first time, the child moved. She stepped off the pavement and into the rain-filled street. The key remained hanging in the air where her hand had been."
